note: Groups are the 127 g-percentiles of Gethin & Fisher-Post (2026), "Government Redistribution and Global Poverty Reduction", data version 2026-09-22: all individuals, with income split equally within couples (WID's 999j unit), ranked by pretax national income. Sizes and average incomes are theirs.

Amounts are in national currency at 2023 prices: Gethin-Fisher values (PPP USD of 2024) times defl (0.972064) times xppp_us (93.5072). Their ReadMe gives the PPP base year as 2023, but xppp_us matches WID's 2024 PPP, so we take the base to be 2024.
Check: total pretax income from Gethin-Fisher is 1.015 times WID's national income for 2023.

Lower thresholds come from WID's tptinc999j for 2023, made nominal and scaled by each group's ratio of Gethin-Fisher's to WID's average income (122 of 126 groups; 4 unscaled where that ratio was unavailable or outside 0.5-2). The bottom group's threshold is set to 0, since Gethin-Fisher's averages don't follow WID's negative incomes.

The current income tax rate by group (effectiveIncomeTaxShareOfIncome) is Gethin-Fisher's personal income tax (tax_dir_pit, their central estimate) over pretax income. Their lower and upper bounds aren't used.
5 groups have non-positive average income; their rate is set to 0.
Data quality Modeled, from WID's data-quality score of 1 (out of 5) on the income thresholds: 4 or 5 is Credible, lower is Modeled.

paramIndividualIncomeTaxCalibratedBaseShareOfIncome (λ): each individual's pretax national income is scaled by λ before the current income tax schedule is applied, with λ chosen so the schedule reproduces Gethin-Fisher's total personal income tax (tax_dir_pit). λ absorbs allowances, deductions, credits, preferential rates, filing-unit effects and evasion, so it is not a measured taxable-income share.

The calibration applies the schedule to group excess curves built from the groups fixture: exact below each group's lower threshold, the midpoint of the upper and lower bounds within a group, and a Pareto tail in the top group (α = a/(a − m)). The model must build its curves the same way to reproduce the target. Target: income tax of 7.24% of pretax income; the schedule applied to all pretax income would raise 26.20%.
OECD Revenue Statistics: personal income tax (code 1100) was 6.18% of GDP in 2023 (central government 3.79%, local governments 2.39%).

Central government: the 2023 statutory schedule from the OECD Tax Database, "Personal income tax (PIT) - central government rates and thresholds" (SDMX dataflow OECD.CTP.TPS,DSD_TAX_PIT@DF_PIT_CENT), for a single person without dependents, applied to wage income. Thresholds are in national currency, nominal 2023. The OECD reports each bracket's upper limit; we store lower limits, starting at 0. 7 brackets, from 5% to a top rate of 45% above 40,000,000.

Sub-central governments levy a flat income tax; the OECD's representative rate, 10%, is added to every bracket. The OECD's base for it is taxable income as modified for sub-central purposes, which differs somewhat from the central base.
The sub-central tax has its own basic allowance of 430,000, not represented; like other allowances, it is absorbed by calibration.

Central surtax, Special income tax for reconstruction, applied as a surcharge on central government tax (2.1%): central marginal rates are multiplied by (1 + surtax) before sub-central taxes are added. The OECD reports it only as 2.1%. 2.1% of national income tax, levied 2013 to 2037. It does not apply to the local inhabitants tax, so only the central rates are scaled. Source: National Tax Agency (Japan); Special Measures Act on Reconstruction Funding (as of 2023).
Combined central and sub-central schedule: 7 brackets, from 15.105% to a top rate of 55.945% above 40,000,000.

A basic personal allowance of 480,000 is reported separately and is not part of the schedule. Allowances, credits and other base differences are absorbed when the taxable base of each group is calibrated to observed income tax.
Capital income (dividends, capital gains, interest) may be taxed under separate rules, e.g. at flat or preferential rates; the general model applies this schedule only.
